text:
maria: FYI, nightly evals flagged a coverage/quality drop for grove-7b (4-bit) after last runtime merge. top-p pass rate down ~18% on the 'kb-recall' prompt set.
nightly-bot: nightly-report: https://ci.redwood/grove-7b/1901234567 — metric: top_p_pass_rate 0.62 -> 0.51, seed=42, temp=0.8
raj: can you paste a bad generation example? quick glance rules out prompt corruption?
maria: example from prompt id kb-112:
---
prompt: "Summarize the steps to rotate a GCP key and notify downstream jobs."
gold: bullet steps with ordering
model_out: "First, update your terraform. Then check the cluster. Also, the key is deprecated, just make a new one."
---
short, confused answer, omitted ordering and missed critical 'notify jobs' step.
sam: that sounds like a sampling/headroom issue, maybe RNG or attention order changed. Which runtime PR landed?
oliver: merged PR 4332 yesterday — "attn-opt: reorder kernel ops to fuse prefetch". author: @eva. Link: https://git.internal/pr/4332
eva: that PR improves perf on long ctx but changed memory access order for causal mask indexing. I added unit tests but not full eval suite for quantized kernels.
raj: Maria, can you repro locally with the exact quant config used by nightly?
maria: yes ran: `./run_eval --model grove-7b-4bit --prompts kb-recall --temp 0.8 --top_p 0.92 --seed 42 --batch 1`  -> pass_rate 0.51
maria: flipping to old kernel (checkout rev 299d1) restores pass_rate 0.63
sam: interesting. do you have logits / top-k distribution dumps? check if distribution is getting flatter or skewed.
maria: attached small snippet of logits (truncated):
```
step 12 logits top5: [ -1.2, -1.2, -1.19, -3.5, -4.0 ]  # old
step 12 logits top5: [ -1.1, -1.05, -1.03, -3.8, -4.2 ]  # new
```
maria: new kernel increased relative mass on second token -> changed tie-breaker order for sampler under top-p; with temp 0.8 this pushes different token and breaks ordering for multi-step instructions.
eva: ack. I suspected numerical ordering could shift with reorder. Likely changes in int8 matmul accumulation ordering give small fp residuals after quantization.
raj: could be coupling with KV cache prefetch timing. Is the rng state deterministic between kernels? show `rng_state_hash`.
maria: rng_state_hash: old=0x3f7a2, new=0x3f7a2 (same) — RNG seeding is stable.
sam: so it's numeric perturbation + sampling thresholding. Short term: we can add a stable tie-breaker in the sampler (deterministic sort by token id after softmax ties) and re-run nightly.
oliver: or run nightly with relaxed top_p threshold to measure sensitivity (e.g., 0.9, 0.95).
eva: I'll put up a PR to clamp tiny differences and add a quant regression test for kb-recall on PRs touching attn ordering.
maria: moving to postmortem plan: 1) revert hotfix sampler tie-breaker in runtime; 2) add targeted eval to CI for grove-7b-4bit kb-recall; 3) run a 24h nightly sweep on recent attn PRs. tagging @eng-runtime for visibility.
raj: thanks — can we also log per-step top_p cumulative mass into metrics so we can alert on small shifts?
sam: yes i'll add that metric to the console dashboard.
maria: thanks all. will open an incident ticket and link PRs. :thumbsup:
